title: Machine-learning-selected variables give parsimonious classifiers for ARDS phenotypes
summary: Random forest, bagging and LASSO selected important variables from three ARDS Network trial cohorts (n=2022), which fed nested logistic regression classifiers of the hyperinflammatory and hypoinflammatory phenotypes. Three-variable (IL-8, bicarbonate, protein C) and four-variable models reached AUC 0.94 and 0.95 in the validation set SAILS (n=715) against latent class analysis labels. The hyperinflammatory phenotype had higher day-90 mortality (39% vs 23%) in the validation set; this is a retrospective secondary analysis with latent-class labels as the reference.
ai_technology: Random forest, bootstrapped aggregating and LASSO for variable selection feeding logistic regression classifiers

evidence.tested: Validation in the SAILS cohort and prognostic checks in two external trial datasets.
evidence.unknown: Prospective validation and real-time biomarker availability; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning algorithms selected the classifier variables.
